title: ErrorDefinition
description:
One error code's definition: the registry entry behind a code such as `meshery-server-1033`. It names the situation the code reports and, for each probable cause, the remediations that answer that cause. A definition is not stored by any server and has no endpoints: the component that owns the code declares it in source (MeshKit's `errors.NewV3`), MeshKit's `errorutil` exports it to the component's `*_errors_index.json`, and docs.meshery.io publishes every definition in an ErrorReferenceIndex. It therefore declares no `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` or `deletedAt`; the code is its key. Causes and remediations are nested, never two parallel lists: each remediation sits under the cause it addresses, and one remediation that answers several causes is repeated under each with the same `id`, so the pairing is explicit and the text is defined once. The flat `probableCause` and `suggestedRemediation` lists earlier consumers read are derived from the nesting (see `probableCause`). The rules JSON Schema cannot state - ids unique, a repeated remediation identical, an `action` behind every `automatic` or `requiresApproval` policy, `code` ending in `-<numericCode>` and the flat lists equal to the derivation - are checked by `Validate` in the generated Go package's helper and by `validateErrorDefinition` in the TypeScript package (docs/error-definition-contract.md).

Projected for sending: upstream's fields only (additionalProperties false).

code.description: The full error code, `<component name>-<numericCode>`, for example `meshery-server-1033`. Codes are scoped to the component that owns them and carry no meaning of their own, so a code is unique only together with its component and nothing may be derived from the number alone.

moniker.description: The name the code has in source, for example `ErrCreatingUUIDInstanceCode` or `ErrApplyManifest`: what MeshKit's export calls `name`. It is not unique across components.

component.description: The component that owns the code.

type.description: The kind of component, for example `component` (Meshery Server), `adapter`, `library` (MeshKit) or `client` (mesheryctl). An open set: a new kind of component needs no schema change.

name.description: The component's name, for example `meshery-server`, `meshkit` or `mesheryctl`. It is the prefix of every code the component owns.

numericCode.description: The number at the end of `code`, as a string of digits so leading zeros survive, for example `1033`. MeshKit's `errorutil` allocates it from the component's `component_info.json` and never reuses it.

severity.description: How severe the error is when it occurs. Omitted when the component assigns none (MeshKit's `None`).

shortDescription.description: One line saying what went wrong, for example `Unable to create UUID instance`. MeshKit's `ShortDescription` lines are joined with `. `. Omitted only for a code whose details the export could not read.

longDescription.description: The full explanation of the error. Omitted when the definition has only text rendered at run time, which MeshKit's `errorutil` cannot export.

probableCauses.description: What may have caused the error, most likely first, each with the remediations that answer it. Cause ids are unique within the definition. Omitted for a definition that documents no causes, such as a code declared with MeshKit's flat `errors.New`, whose flat lists are then the only record (and are unpaired).

items.description: One probable cause of an error, with the remediations that answer it. Remediations are nested under the cause they address, never kept in a parallel list.

id.description: Stable id of the cause, unique within the error's definition, for example `service-not-running`. An event names the causes that apply to one occurrence by this id (`EventError.matchedCauses`), and the docs page links to it, so it never changes once published. Lowercase words joined by hyphens.

description.description: What may have caused the error, for example `The service is not running.`

remediations.description: What answers this cause, the most likely fix first. A remediation that also answers another cause is repeated under that cause with the same `id` and identical fields.

items.description: One remediation for a probable cause: what to do, and optionally a machine-readable action a client may run and the policy that says whether it may run it without asking a person.

id.description: Stable id of the remediation, unique within the error's definition, for example `start-service`. The same id under two causes is one remediation answering both, so its fields must be identical in each place, and the flattened `suggestedRemediation` list carries it once. Lowercase words joined by hyphens.

description.description: What to do, written for a person, for example `Start the service.`

action.description: Identifier of an action a client can run to apply this remediation, as dot-separated lowercase words, for example `service.start` or `connection.reconnect`. The client that runs it owns its meaning; the definition only names it. Omitted when only a person can apply the remediation.

actionPolicy.description: Whether a client may run `action` on its own. `automatic` and `requiresApproval` need an `action`. Omitted means `manual`.

probableCause.description: The flat list of cause descriptions earlier consumers read (MeshKit's `ProbableCause`). When `probableCauses` is present it equals each cause's `description`, in order. Without `probableCauses` it is the definition's only record of its causes, and nothing pairs an entry with an entry of `suggestedRemediation`.

suggestedRemediation.description: The flat list of remediation descriptions earlier consumers read (MeshKit's `SuggestedRemediation`). When `probableCauses` is present it equals every remediation's `description` across the causes, in order, each remediation `id` once (the first time it appears).

referenceUrl.description: The stable docs.meshery.io page for this code, for example `https://docs.meshery.io/reference/error-codes/component-meshery-server/errcreatinguuidinstancecode-1001/`. Always present in a published ErrorReferenceIndex; a component's export may omit it, because the docs build assigns it.
